T5.notes: Study as T3 (Fixed bolt-hole walls, 150 N +X on the bore), on bracket_c.SLDPRT. SF_yield = 45 / 18.60 MPa (peak VM away from the bolt-hole walls, finest local mesh 116,687 nodes); SF_layer = 22.5 / 7.64 MPa where 7.64 is the largest sigma_Y tension over the 0.5-0.25 mm local meshes (sigma_Y is the across-layer stress for this orientation). Same study with the same orientation the other ways: stack along Z gives sigma_Z 16.0 MPa (SF 1.4), stack along X gives sigma_X 13.6 MPa (SF 1.7). The 24-30 MPa peak at the bolt-hole top edges (SF 1.5-1.9) is excluded as a fixed-wall edge effect; a second study with the whole bottom face fixed instead has no such peak and gives VM 17.3 MPa (SF 2.6), sigma_Y 6.6 MPa (SF 3.4). Not checked: layer-to-layer shear, creep, the overhang of the dia 22 bore when printed on its side (needs a teardrop or support), real bolt preload.

T6.solver: SOLIDWORKS Simulation static, frictionless No Penetration contact set (surface-to-surface), Intel direct sparse (set Direct Sparse, reads back swsSolverTypeINTEL=7)
T6.how_pin_was_stabilised: Simulation's soft-spring option (UseSoftSpring2 = True); the pin is otherwise free to slide along Y and rotate about its axis. A coarse (12,752-node) node-to-surface solve with no stabiliser at all gave the same stress, contact pressure (11.56 vs 11.55 MPa) and pin rise (0.135 mm) as with the springs, so the springs do not drive the result; the pin's axial displacement is arbitrary either way (max displacement 70 mm without springs).
T6.why: Peak contact pressure on the hole 6.5 MPa (surface-to-surface, 106,193 nodes). Evidence: (1) equilibrium: bottom-face reaction 500.0 N and normal contact force on the hole 500.08 N for the 500 N applied; (2) surface-to-surface peak pressure over 5,674 / 26,020 / 62,261 / 106,193 nodes = 9.1, 7.6, 6.3, 6.6 MPa, the last step +3.4 %; (3) an independent line-contact (Hertz) hand estimate for a 0.1 mm radial clearance gives 6.8 MPa (a = 1.6 mm, E* = 2.2 GPa, R_eff = 255 mm); (4) pin rise 0.127 mm = the 0.1 mm clearance plus 0.027 mm of local deformation; (5) the soft springs do not change the result. Not fully settled: the node-to-surface formulation on the same meshes does not agree (8.2, 10.1, 13.2, 13.3 MPa and a normal force 495 N, spiky nodal pressures), so the number depends on the contact formulation and I take the surface-to-surface one; block peak von Mises 5.6 MPa sits on the entry edge of the hole at the Y faces and is still creeping up about 2 % per refinement; contact is frictionless, the hole is nominal (no print tolerance), the PETG is isotropic and linear.
